methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Alef Aeronautics is a Series A-stage Transportation company that has raised $30M+ to date. The Transportation sector contains eight private peers of varying stages and scale, including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Pipedream, and FleetZero; no direct public comparables exist in this subsector. A narrow peer-median approach proved inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage datapoints meeting valuation-tier thresholds within Transportation.

Analysis proceeds via stage-progression methodology, applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A-to-subsequent-round advancement. Using the $30M total raised as a proxy valuation baseline, this method implies $60M post-money valuation. This represents a straightforward application of observed funding-round mechanics absent comparable transaction data.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $51M (low) to $69M (high), with a median point of $60M. This range reflects reasonable variance around the stage-progression estimate but remains sensitive to two material uncertainties: (1) the absence of narrow peer transactions limits confidence in the 2.0x multiplier as applied to Alef's specific risk profile and market opportunity; and (2) validation against a broader Transportation peer set could shift the median materially if adjacent-stage or later-stage funding multiples diverge from assumed norms. Additional comparable transaction data or explicit management guidance on capital efficiency would tighten this range.
